_comment: The A/B question set for scripts/mcp-ab: the same maintainer questions
asked of an agent over a Campfire checkout with and without the
roundhouse MCP server attached. Each question carries an answer key
derived from the SOURCE (not from the analyzer), so a run where the tool
misleads the agent scores as wrong, same as a run where grep does.
`expect` are case-insensitive regexes a correct answer contains;
`order` is a list of regexes whose first matches must appear in that sequence (execution order);
`absent` are hallucination tells; `tool` is the roundhouse tool a
well-chosen call would use (measured, never suggested to the agent).

questions.prompt: For the request GET /rooms/:id (RoomsController#show), list every before_action that actually runs, in execution order, naming the file that defines each. Then say which registered filter(s) do NOT run for this action and why. Finally: where does Current.user get assigned during this request?
expect: reject_banned_ip.{0,200}(not run|doesn't run|does not run|won't run|skipped|never runs|is skipped)|(skipped|does not run|not run|doesn't run).{0,200}reject_banned_ip
questions.why: Ruby processes a multi-argument `include` in REVERSE, so ApplicationController's `include AllowBrowser, Authentication, Authorization, BlockBannedRequests, SetCurrentRequest, SetPlatform, TrackedRoomVisit, VersionHeaders` registers VersionHeaders' filter first and AllowBrowser's last. Execution order on GET /rooms/:id: set_version_headers (VersionHeaders), the `Current.request = request` block (SetCurrentRequest), [reject_banned_ip — registered by BlockBannedRequests but `unless: :safe_request?` and a GET is safe, so it does NOT run], require_authentication, deny_bots (Authentication), allow_browser (AllowBrowser), set_room (RoomsController, only: show destroy), [ensure_can_administer — only: destroy, does NOT run], remember_last_room_visited (RoomsController, defined in TrackedRoomVisit). Current.user is set by Current#session= (app/models/current.rb) via require_authentication → restore_authentication → resume_session → authenticated_as. Authorization, SetPlatform, TrackedRoomVisit register no filters themselves.

questions.prompt: In RoomsController#show, can @room be nil at the point app/views/rooms/show.html.erb renders? Explain from how @room is assigned and what happens when the lookup fails.
questions.why: set_room does room_scope.find_by(id: …); on a miss it redirect_to root_url, which halts the filter chain, so show and its view never run with @room nil. A static type of Room? for the ivar is true across the filter body but not at the view.

questions.prompt: In app/views/messages/_message.html.erb, what is the type of `message`, and what is the type of `message.creator`? Can `message.creator` be nil? Say how you determined each.
questions.why: The partial is rendered with a Message; `belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }` — required by default, so a persisted Message has a User creator.

questions.prompt: For the paginated messages feed — MessagesController#index rendering the messages/_message partial (and what it renders) — which associations are preloaded for the messages, and which association reads in the rendered partials would issue a query per message? Name the scopes and the partials involved.
questions.why: find_paged_messages uses only Message.with_creator (preload(creator: :avatar_attachment)). rooms#show adds with_attachment_details and with_boosts; index does not, so the rich-text body / attachment reads and boosts in the partials are per-message reads there — largely masked by the fragment cache in _message.html.erb.

questions.prompt: Suppose this app were compiled to Go with roundhouse. Which declarations in app/models/message.rb would not survive that compilation (are unsupported), as reported by the compiler? List them with line numbers.
questions.why: Only the compiler can answer this; wont_lower(go) reports message.rb:2 include, :9 has_rich_text (as an unsupported assign-target, listed repeatedly), :11 before_create, :12 after_create_commit. (has_one_attached is in message/attachment.rb, outside the file asked about.) Without the tool the honest answer is 'cannot determine' — this question measures a capability the grep arm does not have, not a head-to-head.
